OpenAI and Anthropic now charge for prompt cache writes

Answer: OpenAI and Anthropic both charge for prompt cache writes. OpenAI (GPT-5.6+): 30-minute writes are published on the pricing table (gpt-6-astra $12.50 / 1M) and 12-hour writes are 2.5× uncached input ($25.00 / 1M for astra) per the prompt-caching guide — these are total write rates, not a surcharge on top of input. Anthropic: 5-minute writes are 1.25× input and 1-hour writes are 2× input (Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2.50 / $4.00 per 1M). Cached reads stay cheaper (OpenAI typically 0.1× input; Anthropic 0.1× with model-specific exceptions). Ratecard stores absolute $/1M on each model row and the calculator adds Cache-write MTok/mo when you enter a volume. Checked 2026-11-07.

Key stats
  • OpenAI 30m / 12h (astra): $12.50 / $25.00 per 1M
  • OpenAI rule (GPT-5.6+): 30m ≈ 1.25× input (table); 12h = 2.5× input (prompt-caching guide)
  • Anthropic 5m / 1h (Sonnet 5.5): $2.50 / $4.00 per 1M
  • Anthropic rule: 5m = 1.25× input; 1h = 2× input
  • Cached reads: still discounted (not the same as writes)
  • Calculator: Cache-write MTok/mo + TTL — N/A when a model has no published write price

Questions

Do OpenAI cache writes cost extra?

OpenAI and Anthropic both charge for prompt cache writes. OpenAI (GPT-5.6+): 30-minute writes are published on the pricing table (gpt-6-astra $12.50 / 1M) and 12-hour writes are 2.5× uncached input ($25.00 / 1M for astra) per the prompt-caching guide — these are total write rates, not a surcharge on top of input. Anthropic: 5-minute writes are 1.25× input and 1-hour writes are 2× input (Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2.50 / $4.00 per 1M). Cached reads stay cheaper (OpenAI typically 0.1× input; Anthropic 0.1× with model-specific exceptions). Ratecard stores absolute $/1M on each model row and the calculator adds Cache-write MTok/mo when you enter a volume. Checked 2026-11-07.

What is gpt-6-astra cache-write pricing?

As of 2026-11-07, OpenAI lists gpt-6-astra cache writes at $12.50 per 1M tokens for the 30-minute TTL and $25.00 per 1M for the 12-hour TTL (2.5× its $10 input). Long-context (>272K) writes are $25.00 / $50.00. Source: OpenAI pricing table + prompt-caching guide.

What does Anthropic charge for cache writes?

Anthropic bills 1.25× base input for a 5-minute cache write and 2× base input for a 1-hour write. Example (checked 2026-11-07): Claude Sonnet 5.5 input $2 → 5m $2.50, 1h $4.00 per 1M. Cache reads are typically 0.1× input (0.05× on Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5; 0.025× on Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1). Source: Anthropic pricing docs.

How do I model cache writes in the Ratecard calculator?

Enter Cache-write tokens / month (M) and pick a TTL (Auto uses the short TTL). The write line uses the published absolute $/1M when the model has fields; otherwise it shows N/A. Write rates are total rates — enter only tokens billed as writes, not also in uncached input. Taxes and negotiated discounts are still excluded.

Does Claude’s newer tokenizer change cache-write prices?

No. Anthropic notes that Claude 4.7+ (and Mythos Preview) use a tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens for the same text, which raises billable token counts — it does not change the $/1M cache-write multipliers (still 1.25× / 2× input). Verify token counts on your own prompts.
